title: Changing the email vendor: Checkout must change when it calls the mailer directly, and stays the same when it owns an interface
captions: Design A. Checkout creates an SmtpMailer and calls it. The business code depends on a low-level detail, and it knows how SMTP works.
The company moves to an HTTP email API. The new client takes different arguments, so Checkout must be edited, tested and deployed again.

Design B. The orders module defines a small interface, OrderNotifier, in its own words. Checkout calls only that. SmtpNotifier, a small class that wraps the mailer, implements it. The arrow from the detail now points up.
The vendor changes. A new class, EmailApiNotifier, wraps the new client and implements the same interface. Only one line that wires the objects together changes. Checkout does not.
The same seam lets a test pass in a fake notifier. You can test Checkout without a mail server.
